newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PDVSA hopes to resolve Venezuela shipping crisis.
newsitem.headline: PDVSA hopes to resolve Venezuela shipping crisis.

text.p: State-owned Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) president Luis Giusti said a regional judge's ban on single-hull oil tankers using the Lake Maracaibo shipping channel would have disastrous effects on the Venezuelan economy if it was implemented.
"I think this is something that will be resolved because it would have a terrible effect on Venezuela," Giusti told journalists in Venezuela's Congress.
Asked if PDVSA planned to appeal the decision, which is due to take effect on April 16, he said: "This is something we are dealing with."

Only about 20 percent of the world's tanker fleet has double- hulls or double-bottoms, shipping sources say, so the ruling, if implemented, would drastically increase the cost of transporting crude and therefore reduce the price Venezuela fetches for it.
Judge Ricardo Colmenares made the ruling following a 25,000 barrel oil spill from the single-hulled Nissos Amorgos tanker, which was holed in the Lake Maracaibo shipping channel on February 28.
Only two weeks later, on March 10, the double-hulled Olympic Sponsor went aground in the same spot as the Nissos, but its second skin prevented any spill, shipping sources say.
Giusti said: "We all share concern for the environment and are sorrowed by accidents like the one in Lake Maracaibo, but we also have to be careful about how we formulate preventive measures."

"A ruling like that has a very serious effect on Venezuela's revenues. Anyway, there is no obvious immediate solution because that amount of double-hulled tankers do not exist in the world. In other countries, like the United States, where they are reforming the legislation, they are allowing the time-scale required to modify the fleet and Venezuela ought to, too."
